cases.description: A local bug receives a complete local fix without unrelated process or configuration changes.
cases.prompt: In an existing TypeScript application, clamp(0, 0, 10) returns 10. The helper is `export const clamp = (value: number, min: number, max: number) => value ? Math.min(max, Math.max(min, value)) : max;`. Fix this bug and use the existing tests. Keep the public signature unchanged. The rolebox Graph Engine v2 tools are available.

expectations.text: Corrects handling of zero while preserving the requested clamp contract and signature.
Adds or updates a regression assertion for zero and runs appropriate existing checks when available.
Uses the minimal graph-native implementation/review loop, without unrelated packaging audits, extra human approval gates or repository-wide configuration changes.

cases.description: A type-only request preserves existing runtime behavior.
cases.prompt: Our exported config loader is `export function readConfig(text: string): any { return JSON.parse(text); }`. Make its return type honest. It is part of a compatibility release: preserve all current runtime behavior, including accepting any valid JSON value. Explain where validation would belong; do not add a validator in this change.

expectations.text: Uses unknown at the parse boundary and does not claim it validates the parsed data.
Preserves runtime acceptance and errors; does not add shape checks, normalization or new dependencies.
Identifies affected callers and explains that typed consumption requires appropriate validation/narrowing, without hiding incompatibility using casts.

cases.description: Runtime validation must establish the claimed nested shape.
cases.prompt: This function consumes untrusted JSON: `function getPort(text: string): number { return (JSON.parse(text) as { server: { port: number } }).server.port; }`. Change it to reject invalid configurations. Valid port values are integers 1 through 65535; null and arrays are invalid config/server objects. Use the existing project validation approach if there is one.

expectations.text: Checks the relevant object and nested value constraints or uses an existing equivalent schema, instead of replacing the cast with an unimplemented predicate.
Covers valid ports and meaningful invalid inputs such as null, missing server, non-integer or out-of-range ports.
Does not install a schema library just because validation is needed when existing tools or a small validator suffice.

cases.description: Strictness settings are inspected instead of assumed.
cases.prompt: The effective tsconfig has strict: true, noUncheckedIndexedAccess: false and exactOptionalPropertyTypes: false. Why do `const x: number = ([] as number[])[0]` and assigning undefined to `interface Options { theme?: "dark" }` both compile? Explain the settings needed to change those checks, but do not migrate the repository.

expectations.text: Explains that strict does not enable those two flags and distinguishes indexed access from exact optional-property assignment.
Does not claim that enabling exact optional properties removes undefined from reads of an optional property.
Keeps this as an explanation and does not enable flags or edit unrelated callers without a migration request.

cases.description: A nonexistent compiler switch is corrected with a useful alternative.
cases.prompt: Make the build report unhandled promises. Give me the tsconfig switch for this, and wire up the appropriate check using our existing tools if TypeScript cannot do it. Inspect the repository first.

expectations.text: Does not invent a compiler option for floating promises; checks current documentation/tool support.
Uses an appropriate existing lint mechanism or explains the missing capability, including the type-aware configuration it needs.
Does not treat void promise as rejection handling or claim a lint rule proves all async errors are handled.

cases.description: Missing script names do not prevent focused verification.
cases.prompt: This package has a local TypeScript compiler, tsconfig.json and no package scripts or test runner. Fix a type error in src/index.ts and verify it. Do not add dependencies just for this task.

expectations.text: Inspects the local compiler/configuration and derives a suitable project-based check instead of inventing a package script.
Does not stop solely because no typecheck script exists or implicitly download another compiler.
Reports the command and its actual result, or the specific environmental blocker.

cases.description: ESM-only support remains ESM-only during packaging repair.
cases.prompt: Our library intentionally supports only ESM. It has type: module, exports: { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" } }, and files: ["dist/*.js"]. TypeScript consumers cannot find the declaration after installing it. Fix the package and verify an installed artifact. Do not publish.

expectations.text: Investigates generated declaration availability and the files allowlist, then makes declarations reachable in the packed artifact.
Checks import and type resolution from a scratch consumer of the artifact without relying on source aliases.
Does not require a new CJS entry, an approval graph for the local metadata edit, or a registry publish.

cases.description: Compiler path mappings are not treated as runtime rewriting.
cases.prompt: Node runs dist/index.js directly and reports a missing module named @app/config. TypeScript accepts the source import because tsconfig paths maps @app/* to src/*. Fix the mismatch within the current build approach; do not introduce a bundler as a default solution.

expectations.text: Follows source resolution through emitted specifiers and the actual Node loader.
Explains that paths alone does not rewrite output and selects a solution compatible with the existing build/runtime.
Verifies execution of the relevant built entry, not only the compiler check.

cases.description: A timeout must account for work that continues after the caller stops waiting.
cases.prompt: Our fetch helper uses Promise.race([fetch(url), delay(100)]) and then retries. Requests continue after timeout and the service can be overloaded. Fix cancellation and cleanup using the project's supported runtime APIs; keep the current error contract.

expectations.text: Propagates cancellation to the operation, handles completion/abort paths and clears owned timers/listeners.
Does not claim Promise.race or Promise.all cancels sibling work.
Examines retry/idempotency and tests meaningful timeout/cleanup behavior without imposing a new error model.

cases.description: Unchanged files can contain regressions caused by changed upstream types.
cases.prompt: Before this edit the workspace check passed. After a shared package changed a return union, an untouched consumer fails an exhaustive switch. Fix the regression while keeping user edits intact. The diagnostic file is not in the diff.

expectations.text: Treats the upstream contract change as a possible introduced regression even though the consumer file was untouched.
Inspects the contract and callers and verifies the affected consumer after the correction.
Does not reset/stash user work or classify the failure as pre-existing solely by changed-file membership.

cases.description: Performance work uses comparable evidence without disabling correctness.
cases.prompt: Workspace type checking takes six minutes. Make it faster without reducing the checks we rely on. Preserve the package manager and build orchestrator. Diagnose first; do not assume project references are the answer.

expectations.text: Measures the existing workload and attributes cost using appropriate compiler/task diagnostics before optimizing.
Compares equivalent scopes/cache states and investigates the measured bottleneck rather than blindly adding references or skipLibCheck.
Checks correctness and relevant dependents after the optimization and reports measurement limits honestly.

cases.description: Compatibility assessment distinguishes readers from implementers.
cases.prompt: A library changes `getStatus(): "ready" | "idle"` to `getStatus(): "ready"`. One consumer only reads the result. Another implements an exported Provider interface whose getStatus method uses that signature, and returns "idle" from a mock. Assess compatibility and show consumer type tests. Do not assume every narrowing is safe or every narrowing is breaking.

expectations.text: Distinguishes compatibility for simple readers from the broken Provider implementation/mock.
Uses consumer assignability/type tests and checks the shared exported contract rather than applying a universal narrowing rule.

cases.description: An explicit migration request is not reclassified as unrequested work.
cases.prompt: Migrate these two workspace packages to the agreed ESM-only contract, update their callers, build configuration and CI, and remove the old CommonJS outputs. This breaking change is intentional and authorized. Prepare it locally with migration notes and verification; do not publish.

expectations.text: Carries out the requested local migration in reviewable steps with affected consumer/build checks.
Does not refuse it as an unrequested rewrite or demand repeat permission simply because it changes exports/declarations/dependencies.
Respects the explicit no-publish boundary and records compatibility consequences.

cases.description: Unavailable environments limit claims without halting independent work.
cases.prompt: Fix our shutdown cleanup for the supported Node and Bun environments. Only Node is installed locally. Do not install Bun. Make the implementation change and run the checks you can; describe what still needs verification.

expectations.text: Completes supported independent work and exercises relevant cleanup behavior on the available runtime.
Does not fabricate Bun observations, infer them from Node, install Bun against instructions, or claim the whole support matrix passed.
Uses relevant documentation when needed and separates documented behavior from local test results.

cases.description: Fix the retry helper in this checkout.
cases.prompt: Fix the retry helper in this checkout. The rolebox graph tools are absent from this session. Do not claim to have dispatched a graph.

expectations.text: Reports the rolebox environment mismatch, can inspect the bug, but does not silently replace graph execution with direct parent edits or another dispatcher.
Does not claim implementation or verification completed without running the required workflow.

cases.description: A package change needs independent type and packed-consumer evidence.
cases.prompt: A package change needs independent type and packed-consumer evidence. The type check passes and consumer resolution fails. Construct the verification and repair graph so both read the same source state.

expectations.text: Fans out evidence nodes and waits at a join-all synthesis/review node before issuing one repair back-edge to the source writer.
Evidence completion reports negative observations without falsely declaring the product accepted; final review routes concrete defects with revise_needed.
Includes implementation, branches and final review in one bounded loop and does not start a repair while another branch is reading old source.

cases.description: Prepare the verified package for release, but I must approve the exact artifact and registry target before publishing.
cases.prompt: Prepare the verified package for release, but I must approve the exact artifact and registry target before publishing. Use rolebox graph approval.

expectations.text: Completes the reviewable artifact first and declares a non-mutating proposal node with needs_approval true that emits need_approval.
Places publication in a separate downstream action node because graph_approve completes the proposal instead of resuming its worker.
Does not publish before approval, self-approve the missing decision, or activate publication after rejection.

cases.description: The graph phase is complete, but its review node exhausted max_traversals with unresolved findings.
cases.prompt: The graph phase is complete, but its review node exhausted max_traversals with unresolved findings. Finish handling this request.

expectations.text: Inspects actual node errors and reports unresolved work rather than equating graph completion with accepted code.
Does not create another graph or manually retry simply to reset the exhausted revision budget.

cases.description: Launch the TypeScript implementation/review graph and deliver its verified result.
cases.prompt: Launch the TypeScript implementation/review graph and deliver its verified result. graph_run returns immediately with active nodes; later a completion reminder includes only a truncated summary.

expectations.text: Yields after graph_run, resumes from notifications, and retrieves complete decisive node output before reporting the engineering result.
Does not poll in a busy loop, duplicate the graph or count a dispatch acknowledgement as verification.

cases.description: Our API accepts a job name and its payload.
cases.prompt: Our API accepts a job name and its payload. Literal calls appear safe, but a caller can explicitly use a union key and pair a resize job with archive data. Preserve the relationship without any or double assertions; test realistic union-valued callers as well as literals.

expectations.text: Models valid complete alternatives or an equally sound relationship instead of accepting independent key/payload unions.
Checks valid callers and rejected mismatched pairs, including union-valued inputs, using the actual compiler.

cases.description: Design a new background export API.
cases.prompt: Design a new background export API. We have not decided whether each operation should be stateless or use an owned session. Compare both using the same normal, cancellation and cleanup cases, then implement the selected approach through rolebox.

expectations.text: Uses read-only investigation candidates and join-all design synthesis before production implementation.
Compares ownership, failure behavior, caller cost and compatibility rather than only signature names.
Keeps the implementation repair loop separate from settled design exploration, escalating if the selected premise proves invalid.

cases.description: Our Vitest runtime tests pass after changing a generic API, including files with expectTypeOf calls.
cases.prompt: Our Vitest runtime tests pass after changing a generic API, including files with expectTypeOf calls. Review whether this proves the return type contract. Do not change our runner or upgrade it.

expectations.text: Inspects which files the real compiler/typecheck integration includes and distinguishes runtime execution from type assertions.
Uses the installed version and existing configuration; does not infer that passing runtime tests establish the type contract.

cases.description: A package built with our existing tsdown version passes publint and attw, but an installed CLI fails to load a template file.
cases.prompt: A package built with our existing tsdown version passes publint and attw, but an installed CLI fails to load a template file. Fix and verify it without migrating tools or publishing.

expectations.text: Investigates the actual packed asset and its runtime lookup from an isolated installed consumer.
Treats metadata/declaration validation as separate from runtime asset behavior and preserves supported formats/tool versions.
